title: Concerning the Fifty Lord's Days; to what Mysteries do they correspond? Or the Second (Fifty); to whose Sign (are they)?
teaching_text:
Once [again] a disciple stood up. He questions the apostle, saying to him: I beseech you, my master, to recount to us about the fifty lord's days during which the catechumens fast. For what do they fast, or for whose mystery do they fast? Or these second (fifty) that is set between the elect, to whose mystery were they set amongst them? Proclaim this also to [us] and persuade us about it, because [ ... / ... ] you [ ... ]

Then [he] says to his questioner and they with him: Happen you know that [in eac]h one of these five garments that the [First] Man summoned there are five powers. They shall be counted to the [ ... each] other, these five, and five times [ ... ] their number. However, at the time [ ... ] the summons went down. The answer wished to ascend with it. And the summons with the obedience [constitute] twenty-five characteristics in their twenty-five limbs, [which] are the sons of the Man. The summons and [the obed]ience were raised to the heights through them.

⟨p.263⟩ Just as their fa[ther] the living Man raised himself up through them, by these these other ones have set up all things a[bov]e and below. Indeed, these are what are called pentecost, the fifty great days that are the [archetypes of the] holy [d]ays. They fasted from their [foo]d, [w]hich is their own.

So, from that time until [the time] of [the adv]ent of Jesus the Splendour, the glorious one who came [ ... / ... t]heir food which is the [ ... ] of sou[l], which is the summons and the obedience [ ... ] that spiritual food. They rele[ased ... ] all these fifty days, which [ ... ] this living food suffices for all of them. It filled them all with power and richness and life. Light [ ... ] this living food that [ ... ] became rich.

They ceased being fifty days. [They] have gone. They became the one hundred holy days that are the fifty [d]ays [ ... ] fast [ ... / ... ] that they have joined them wit[h them / ... ] these mysteries of these first fifty [ ... ] these second (fifty) also [in] which the elect [fast] correspond to the sign of the fifty [ ... ] the summons and the obedience set them in their splendrous [places] at the coming of Jesus.

⟨p.264⟩ Now, behold, these are the [great] days of the fifty lord's days that I have revealed [for the] catechumens. Behold, these are the fifty da[ys of] the second (group) that I have revealed for the elec[t ... ] You enquire about these mysteries. They also occur in [the teachin]gs of the sects. They have fifty days in which they f[as]t. They call them penteco[st], because the apostles themselves fasted for these fifty days, they revealed them to their disciples.

Also, {Chr]ist himself revealed these fifty days to [them] on [the d]ay, fasting on the mountain, at the time when the [de]vi[l] tempted him. He spent another seven days g[oing i]n [to] the house [of Simon] the leper, together with the three other [days t]hat he [spent] in the sepulchre among the dead.

Yet, [ ... in these f]ifty days. And I, I have b[estowed them] on the entire church with these fifty days in which the catechu[m]ens fast, after the myster[y of the] First Man. And the other fifty, after the sign of the s[ec]ond man who was revealed in the church.
gardner_synopsis:
Mani is asked to explain the significance of the fifty fasts undertaken by the catechumens, that is once weekly on each lord's day; and also of a further fifty held by the elect. He engages in some rather convoluted calculations to reach these totals.

The first fifty correspond to the mystery of the First Man: five powers for each of his five sons or garments equals twenty-five limbs of the living soul. This divine son/s of the Man (note the deliberate Christological reference) has abstained from the food of life in a world of mixture. The doubling of the twenty-five seems (263.4 - 9?) to be calculated with reference to the ascent of the First Man; and then the ascent of the call and answer, which are the counsel of life or means of salvation for the soul.

The second fifty correspond to the mystery of Jesus as the second man: forty days fasting in the desert, seven days in the house of Simon the leper, and three in the tomb.

footnotes.text: Smagina 1990:122 suggests that the term δευτέρα stands for Monday, i.e. the second day of the week upon which the elect fasted.

editorial_notes: Removed manuscript line-number intrusions (e.g., 15, 20, 25, etc.) from the running translation while retaining meaningful numerals (e.g., fifty, one hundred, twenty-five). Removed Coptic line-break slashes “/” and re-joined broken words where possible (e.g., “apo15stl [e]” → “apostle”; “wh/ich” → “which”; “sum- mons” → “summons”; “sou [1, w]hich” → “soul, which”). Deleted modern page headers/running titles and standalone print-page numbers (e.g., 269, 270; “THE KEPHALAIA OF THE TEACHER”). Converted manuscript page markers “(263)” and “(264)” to ⟨p.263⟩ and ⟨p.264⟩. Footnote markers were removed from the teaching text and collected separately. Some OCR damage remains where the English was itself fragmentary or where brackets indicate lacunae/restoration (e.g., “{Chr]ist”).
